Unlike many of your peers, who have aspirations for further studies, this lack of ambition may be contributing to the prediction of failure. Additionally, your history of past class failures is another critical element; having one failure already places you at a disadvantage compared to students who have not experienced any setbacks.

Another factor is the reason you chose this school. Many students select their schools based on course offerings or reputation, while your choice was primarily based on proximity to home. This could suggest a lack of engagement or motivation that might affect your academic performance.

To improve your chances of success, consider taking proactive steps. Engaging more deeply with your studies, seeking extra help, and participating in additional educational support can make a significant difference. It may also be beneficial to explore your interests and motivations for higher education, as this can inspire a more focused approach to your studies. By addressing these areas, you can enhance your academic performance and work towards passing your final year.
